title: Recursive Monte-Carlo Tree Search
claim: Exploration-driven upper confidence bound values fluctuate erratically and converge slowly, so the arm with the lower true reward is still selected.
layout: 1 panel, single line plot, two colored curves, legend top-right
description: A single matplotlib line chart titled 'UCB Values over Simulations'. The x-axis is simulations from 0 to 200. The y-axis is UCB value, from about -0.5 to 1.7. Two curves are shown: blue for an arm with p = 0.4 and orange for an arm with p = 0.6, with a legend in the top-right corner. The orange curve spikes to about 1.7 early, then drops and oscillates before settling near 0.35. The blue curve starts at about -0.5 and rises, with sawtooth jumps and sharp drops at the points where that arm is chosen. Both curves converge toward 0.3 to 0.4 by 200 simulations. The eye goes first to the tall early orange peak, then to the blue sawtooth pattern.
caption: Illustration of UCB values over 200 simulations in bandit
abstract: We introduce a recursive AlphaZero style Monte--Carlo tree search algorithm, "RMCTS". It first generates the search tree using prior policies, and then recursively re-estimates action values by using the regularized optimal posterior policies from ``Monte--Carlo tree search as regularized policy optimization'' (Grill et al., 2020) at each node of the search tree, starting from the leaves and working back up to the root. We find that RMCTS matches or exceeds the quality of AlphaZero's MCTS-UCB in a tiny fraction of the time.
